title: Qatar PM Sheikh Mohammed Visits Tehran in First High-Level Qatari Trip Since War Began, Pushes Hormuz De-Escalation
detail: Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani traveled to Tehran on Aug 27 — the first high-level Qatari visit to Iran since the war began Feb 28 — meeting Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, and Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei. Discussions centered on the proposed phased Strait of Hormuz plan (temporary shipping corridor plus joint mine-clearing project), freedom of navigation, and creating conditions for a resumption of US-Iran dialogue. Sheikh Mohammed said Qatar 'believes that dialogue and diplomatic solutions remain the optimal path for addressing disputes,' stressing 'the need to respect the sovereignty of neighbouring countries and freedom of navigation.' Rezaei countered that 'the US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz.' Qatar — host to the US Al Udeid Air Base and a shared gas field with Iran — has served as a back-channel mediator throughout the war and helped broker the June ceasefire; its own LNG exports have collapsed from 509 cargoes pre-war to just 18 recently amid the shipping disruption.

media.caption: Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani meets Iranian officials in Tehran, Aug 27, 2026

title: DOJ Moves to Revive Civil War-Era Maritime Prize Courts to Seize Iranian Oil Tankers
detail: The Justice Department is preparing to reactivate long-dormant maritime 'prize courts' — last used in the Spanish-American War era — to streamline the legal confiscation of Iranian oil tankers captured under the US naval blockade, with proceeds from sold oil and cargo routed to the Treasury. Aaron Reitz, US Attorney for the Southern District of Texas (identified as the venue given its port and maritime infrastructure), confirmed DOJ is 'now reviving' the mechanism: 'Prize law is an ancient body of maritime law — already codified in statute but which we are now reviving — that sets the rules for how seized maritime property is condemned, returned or disposed of.' The plan aims to shield the US from third-party claims and accelerate liquidation of seized Iranian assets, offsetting the war's costs, but is expected to draw legal challenges from shipping companies and other claimants against the seized vessels and cargo.

media.caption: An oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, as DOJ moves to revive Civil War-era prize courts to seize Iranian tankers

confidenceReason: Confirmed on-record by the lead US Attorney involved, but the plan remains unfinalized policy, not yet in force.

title: Iran-Oman Hormuz Accord Status Disputed Internally as Trump Says US 'Not in a Hurry' to Resume Talks
detail: A day after IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said Iran and Oman had reached agreement on their respective shares of Strait of Hormuz waters and revenues ('we have been in negotiations with Oman for about a month, and we have reached results that are acceptable to both sides'), a senior Iranian official told Reuters the accord 'has not been finalised' and that talks on the details were continuing — leaving unclear at what stage the reported agreement actually stands. Mohebbi added that 'if the United States stops obstructing and returns to the agreement, we can open the Strait within the framework,' reiterating Iran's conditions of ending the naval blockade, compensation, and sanctions relief. Separately, President Trump told Al Jazeera on Aug 26 he has 'no time schedule, none — I'm not in a hurry' for Iran to return to talks, claiming 'we are winning very big' and that both economic pressure and military strikes have been 'effective.' Outgoing White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt reiterated Thursday morning that 'no negotiations are happening right now, and this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way,' adding Iran is 'in a devastating place. Inflation is over 100%. They can't pay their police,' while calling the naval blockade 'hugely successful.'

media.caption: President Trump, who told Al Jazeera he is 'not in a hurry' for Iran to return to talks, Aug 26, 2026
